narrative.overview: yarr is a clean, just-the-facts instrument — a Bloomberg terminal for the feeds you chose. It is not a magazine, not a discovery engine, not a place to linger over chrome. The whole surface exists to move a backlog of unread items past your eyes quickly, let you keep the few that matter, and get out of the way. Density and speed are the aesthetic; the interface should feel like a well-worn CLI that happens to have a screen — instant, predictable, unsurprising. Three columns carry the desktop experience (feeds → items → article), collapsing to one at a time on a phone with no duplicate markup. There is exactly one accent color, and it never decorates — it only signals state.
keyCharacteristics: Information-dense, three-pane terminal that collapses to single-pane on mobile.
One accent (Signal Blue), used only for state — selection, active, focus.
Three first-class themes; every surface must read in all three.
Keyboard is a primary path, not a power-user extra; visible focus is required.
Flat by default; lift is reserved for the triage card and the undo toast.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is the only accent and it only ever means state — selected, active, focused, or a link. Orange means one thing (Instapaper); red means one thing (error/offline). Three functional colors, zero decorative ones.

rules.name: The Filled-State Rule
rules.body: When white text sits on the accent (selected row, active filter), use Signal Blue Deep (#0067ab), not Signal Blue — #fff on #0080d4 is only ~3.9:1 and fails AA.

rules.name: The Three-Equal-Themes Rule
rules.body: Light, sepia, and night are equal citizens. Any new surface must be designed and contrast-checked in all three before it ships.

rules.name: The No-Display-Face Rule
rules.body: UI labels, buttons, and data never use a display or decorative font. Hierarchy comes from weight and size on one sans.

rules.name: The Reader-Only Serif Rule
rules.body: Georgia and the mono stack appear only in the article reading pane as a user preference; never in chrome.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadow is reserved for the two objects that float over content (triage card, undo toast) and hairline pressable affordances.

rules.name: The One Selection Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: Selected/active looks the same everywhere — accent fill, white text — so the eye learns it once.

dos: Do keep Signal Blue (#0080d4) for state only, and reach for Signal Blue Deep (#0067ab) whenever white text sits on the accent.
Do design and contrast-check every new surface in light, sepia, AND night before shipping; AA (4.5:1 body) is the floor.
Do keep chrome to the 2rem toolbar band (3rem mobile) and a single 1px divider.
Do give every interactive element a full keyboard path and a visible :focus-visible ring.
Do provide a prefers-reduced-motion alternative for every animation.
Do keep one type family in chrome; build hierarchy from weight and size.
Do keep touch targets >=44px on mobile.
donts: Don't add promoted content, discover rails, engagement nudges, or celebratory confetti/emoji. yarr is not Feedly.
Don't drift the themes toward the AI-cream aesthetic — no warm-neutral paper backgrounds, no tracked-uppercase eyebrows, no identical icon-heading-text card grids.
Don't introduce a second accent or use the accent decoratively.
Don't use a display or decorative font anywhere in the UI; serif/mono live only inside the reader pane.
Don't add drop shadows for looks. Flat by default; only the triage card and undo toast float.
Don't use border-left/border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe.
Don't ship a surface that's legible in light but muddy in sepia or night.
